name: AI Courses
blurb: University and platform courses, with duration, cost, and what they actually teach.

items.cost: Free to audit; certificate fee listed on page
items.name: AI for Everyone
items.note: A non-technical course on what AI can and cannot do inside an organisation
items.audience: Managers, executives and anyone working alongside technical teams

items.name: CS224n: NLP with Deep Learning
items.note: The NLP counterpart to CS231n, updated through the transformer era

items.name: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
items.note: The vision course that trained a generation; lectures, notes, and assignments public

items.name: CS285: Deep Reinforcement Learning
items.note: Sergey Levine's graduate RL course, lectures and homework public

items.name: Deep Learning Specialization
items.note: Five courses from dense networks through sequence models; the standard second step

items.name: AI Engineering in Python
items.note: A project-based learning path with a completion certificate, not a proctored exam
items.audience: Career changers who want to learn by building projects

items.name: Generative AI Fundamentals in Python
items.note: A short project-based path with a completion certificate, not a proctored exam
items.audience: Developers who want hands-on practice with LLM APIs

items.name: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
items.note: Code-first: you train real models in lesson one and earn the theory afterward

items.name: Machine Learning Crash Course
items.note: Google's refreshed MLCC with interactive visuals and Keras exercises

items.name: Hugging Face Learn (LLM, Agents, Diffusion courses)
items.note: Hands-on courses on transformers, agents, and diffusion using the Hub itself

items.name: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
items.note: From backprop by hand to a working GPT, on video, building everything live
items.audience: Engineers who want to build GPT from scratch

items.name: MIT 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
items.note: MIT's annual bootcamp; every January's lectures posted free with labs

items.name: Machine Learning Specialization
items.note: Andrew Ng's rebuilt classic; the most common starting point in the field

reading.body:
All ten courses tracked here offer free access to their core materials, though three, DeepLearning.AI's specializations and Karpathy's and fast.ai's courses, pair that with either a paid certificate option or accompanying public code repositories.

Four are university graduate courses with public materials, Stanford's CS224n and CS231n, UC Berkeley's CS285, and MIT's 6.S191, while the rest come from industry, DeepLearning.AI, Google, Hugging Face, fast.ai, and independent researcher Andrej Karpathy. That split matters because university courses are generally structured around exam-driven theory while the industry courses here are described as code-first or hands-on, meaning the choice between them is really a choice about how someone wants to learn rather than which source is more rigorous.

Only three courses list an accompanying public code repository, fast.ai, Karpathy's Zero to Hero, and MIT's 6.S191, which the data flags directly through the with_code count. The data does not report enrollment numbers, completion rates, or which of these ten is most widely taken.
